title: FindSG · Story Scene Visuals
art_direction: Hand-drawn architectural concept vectors, keeping four distinct visual languages: paper, printer's ink, film and night-time timekeeping.
accuracy_note: All buildings, objects, streets and routes are drawn as recognisable concepts — not exact elevations, survey maps or real historical images.
motion_note: Readable as a still; plays once only when the parent page adds is-playing, and respects prefers-reduced-motion.

routes.title: Letters to the Shore

ability.title: Observation Card
ability.effect: Highlights “voyage” and “Mazu” in the Thian Hock Keng evidence, helping you find the first generation's wish.
ability.grant_rule: At Stop 4, fill both shape slots in turn — square for the base, octagon for the upper tier — to claim the Observation Card ×1.
ability.use_feedback: Observation Card used: two keywords light up. It's up to you how they connect to “arrive safely”.
ability.unchanged_core: You still choose how the wish matches the history, and read or say one sentence of explanation.
ability.label: Prototype ability card

routes.fiction_note: The family letters, characters, seals, ledger pages, annotations, time windows, AI judgements and level passwords are all fiction created for this project; we don't claim that real venues hold these objects or ever passed this letter along together. Only each stop's historical_fact and its sources are researched history; no real religious site is cast as a secret society, curse or criminal group.

routes.title: The Last Edition

ability.title: Proofing Card
ability.effect: Strikes one mismatched relationship from the fictional subscription list at the next stop, leaving two links for you to judge.
ability.grant_rule: At Stop 4, put the 111, JALAN and SULTAN blocks in the right order, choose the mirrored plate and make a successful test print to claim the Proofing Card ×1.
ability.use_feedback: Proofing Card used: the line that mistook the printing house for the school's founder has been struck out. Keep comparing the remaining two.
ability.unchanged_core: You still need to identify the historical fact that charity supported the school, and to sort out the fictional subscription links.
ability.label: Prototype ability card

routes.fiction_note: Ah Ming, the time travel, the blank paper, the mission dialogue and the layout codes are all fiction. 1938 is the fictional character’s year of departure, not a claim that every building on the route existed then. Each fact card states its own date; the 3D print room is an artistic reconstruction.

routes.title: The Last Screening: The Deleted Credits

ability.title: Editing Card
ability.effect: At the water kiosk, place the “free water” and “passers-by” evidence side by side so you can see one relationship in daily life.
ability.grant_rule: At Stop 4, open the 1926 and 1928 records first, then pick the shared developer, Sim Cheng Neo, from the candidate credits to earn Editing Card ×1.
ability.use_feedback: Editing Card used: water and passers-by now share one frame. What the blank bill means is still yours to decide.
ability.unchanged_core: You still have to tell gift, sale and loan apart, and must not treat the fictional bill as a real charity record.
ability.label: Prototype ability card

routes.fiction_note: Mariam, the Time Camera, the plea footage, the missing credits, all character dialogue and all fictional props are invented. There is no evidence that the seven places took part in one event; we do not claim to have found a real lost film, nor attribute any case or crime to real historical figures. Numbers, subtitles and route hints on the game screen are not real inscriptions on site. Public exteriors and historical facts ground the story, but artistic 3D reconstructions are not exact historical restorations.

routes.title: The Missing Years: Recovering the City's 25 Years

ability.title: Boost Card
ability.effect: At Tan Kim Seng Fountain, sort the three file pages in one go — the donor, the 1857 donation and the 1882 memorial fountain — saving three manual placements.
ability.grant_rule: At Stop 7, complete the three driving segments in turn — accelerate, brake, exit the corner — to collect Boost Card ×1. There is no countdown; keyboard and buttons earn the same reward.
ability.use_feedback: Boost Card used: the three file pages slot into place. 1857 and 1882 light up together; the 25 years are still yours to explain.
ability.unchanged_core: It will not choose the 25 years for you, nor skip telling the donation apart from the memorial.
ability.label: Prototype ability card

routes.fiction_note: The file restorer, every year turning into 2026, the calibration cards, the three English words in the race and the timer fault are all original fiction. Real people are not given unevidenced private conversations or secret actions. Historical facts follow each stop's source_urls. The existing 3D game has not been consulted or connected, so we do not assume its track year, assets, code, interfaces or completion callbacks are compatible with this plan.

scenes.action: Put the 1857 donation and the 1882 memorial back in their own years.
scenes.feedback: The 25 years return to the timer; the ending keeps both events apart and invents no construction time.

hotspots.label: Read the history clue
hotspots.detail: In 1857 Tan Kim Seng donated $13,000 to improve the public water supply; the fountain in his memory was erected in 1882. The building is drawn as a concept vector, not an exact reconstruction.

hotspots.label: See the story action
hotspots.detail: The letters, dialogue, captions and puzzle mechanics here are story creations; historical facts keep the sources on their original cards.

units.name: Fuk Tak Chi Museum
units.design_note: A temple entrance and exhibit labels express the shrine-turned-museum's two identities; real displays are not reproduced.
units.historical_fact: Founded in 1824 by Hakka and Cantonese migrants as a small shrine that also served as a community mutual-aid centre; converted into a museum in 1998.

units.name: Ying Fo Fui Kun
units.design_note: Eaves, doors and windows are simplified concepts; the five-point network stands for the five-county community and is not original decoration.
units.historical_fact: Founded in 1822 to serve Hakka migrants from five counties in Guangdong; the association still stands on its original Telok Ayer site.

units.name: Nagore Dargah Indian Muslim Heritage Centre
units.design_note: Emphasises the twin-tower outline from the records; no tomb is drawn, and the number of tiers is not a survey fact.
units.historical_fact: A memorial to a saint built by the South Indian Chulia community; no saint's remains are buried here. Since 2011 it has housed the Indian Muslim Heritage Centre.

units.name: Former Keng Teck Whay Building / Singapore Yu Huang Gong
units.design_note: Square and octagon form comparable volumes; the original building's completion year is not inferred.
units.historical_fact: Keng Teck Whay was founded in 1831 by 36 Peranakan Chinese merchants as a private mutual-aid society; its original building later became Yu Huang Gong.

units.name: Thian Hock Keng
units.design_note: Temple eaves and voyage labels sit on separate layers; the labels are story props, and no deities or worshippers are drawn.
units.historical_fact: Where Hokkien migrants prayed to Mazu for safe voyages; the present large temple was built in 1839–1842 and also hosted clan association and education activities.

units.name: Chong Wen Ge
units.design_note: The books are an education-theme object; they do not claim the interior still holds this arrangement.
units.historical_fact: Tan Kim Seng led its building in 1849, with donations from the Hokkien, Hakka and Teochew communities; the neighbouring Chong Hock Pavilion opened Chong Hock Girls' School in 1915.

units.name: Al-Abrar Mosque
units.design_note: Distinguished from Nagore's tiered twin towers by its narrow frontage and central entrance.
units.historical_fact: Began as a thatched hut in 1827 and became a permanent building in 1855, serving the South Indian Chulia community; its narrow façade has two minaret-like features.

units.name: Telok Ayer Chinese Methodist Church
units.design_note: Composed from the mixed architectural features in existing records; not a full construction drawing.
units.historical_fact: The congregation began in 1889 and the present building was completed in 1925; a Chinese pavilion sits atop a Western building, and it sheltered about 300 people during the Second World War.

units.name: Bussorah Street · former Kampong Kaji stretch
units.design_note: The street perspective is a concept composition; the luggage and ship tickets are everyday-life objects.
units.historical_fact: A stretch near Sultan Mosque was once called Kampong Kaji, where pilgrims from the region waited for ships, lodged and prepared for the journey.

units.name: Gedung Kuning
units.design_note: Shown as a detached yellow house; the residents' ethnicity is not inferred from the building's look.
units.historical_fact: Gedung Kuning was long a family home. Javanese merchant Haji Yusoff bought it in 1912; it was later sold, then bought back.

units.name: Aliwal Arts Centre · former Chong Cheng School and Chong Pun Girls’ School
units.design_note: The two wings and shared hall show a relationship, not a navigable floor plan.
units.historical_fact: This building once housed two Chinese schools — boys in one wing, girls in the other, sharing a hall. The facade records the year it was built and its donors.

units.name: The Sultan · former Al-Ahmadiah and HARMY Press
units.design_note: A concept pairing of old printing and today's building; it does not claim a real press stands at the door.
units.historical_fact: No. 101 was once the Al-Ahmadiah and HARMY Press and is now The Sultan hotel; the old building is a remnant of Kampong Gelam’s publishing network.

units.name: Madrasah Alsagoff Al-Arabiah
units.design_note: The address 111 is used for the digital label; the fictional subscription slip is not treated as a real school record.
units.historical_fact: The school was founded in 1912 and is linked to the Alsagoff family from Hadhramaut, Yemen, and their charitable support.

units.name: Malabar Mosque
units.design_note: Uses the building's later colours from existing records, not its original look at the 1963 opening.
units.historical_fact: The mosque was championed by the Malabar Muslim community from Kerala and opened in 1963; the blue walls and golden dome were added later.

units.name: Istana Kampong Gelam · Malay Heritage Centre
units.design_note: The building is a concept outline; the 2026 reopening stays on the fact card, and no on-site plaque is faked.
units.historical_fact: The former palace is now the Malay Heritage Centre, which reopened on 25 April 2026.

units.name: Goh Chor Tua Pek Kong Temple and the old opera stage
units.design_note: The two spaces sit side by side and the 1847 and 1906 events stay separate; no performance on the day is shown as visual fact.
units.historical_fact: Founded in 1847 by Hokkien labourers from the sugar-cane plantations; the permanent stage beside it was built by Tan Boo Liat in 1906.

units.name: Sim Kwong Ho Shophouses
units.design_note: The façade outline and the name card are kept apart; the developer is not the building's name.
units.historical_fact: Sim Cheng Neo developed these shophouses in 1926; the building name comes from the words Sim Kwong Ho on the corner facade.

units.name: Lam Yeo Coffee Powder Factory
units.design_note: Coffee sacks and newspapers are concept objects for changing trades; no product packaging is copied.
units.historical_fact: The founder was once an assistant editor at the Nanyang Siang Pau, sold coffee on the street in 1959 and opened a shop with his wife in 1960; Lam Yeo means Nanyang.

units.name: Kwan Yow Luen Shophouses
units.design_note: Brings out the rhythm of the terrace façade, distinct from the corner shophouses; no real film stills are invented.
units.historical_fact: Developed by Sim Cheng Neo in 1928 and designed by Kwan Yow Luen, this row of shophouses once appeared in a P. Ramlee film.

units.name: Boon Teck Road Water Kiosk
units.design_note: The vessels are a water-giving concept; the number of vessels or drinks on any given day is not guaranteed.
units.historical_fact: The related charitable halls merged in 1950 and long offered free water and herbal tea to passers-by; NHB records that the water kiosk was kept at this junction.

units.name: Maha Sasanaramsi Burmese Buddhist Temple
units.design_note: The roofs are simplified; no Buddha image details are drawn, and the 1991 move to this site is kept apart from the original temple's dates.
units.historical_fact: The original temple was set up on Kinta Road in 1878, and the temple at the present site was completed in 1991; the marble Buddha was already enshrined at the old temple in 1921.

units.name: Former Malay Film Productions Studio
units.design_note: The entrance and equipment are film-theme concepts; real interiors that are not open to visitors are not shown.
units.historical_fact: The Jalan Ampas studio resumed production in 1947, bringing together Chinese producers, Indian directors and Malay actors; it closed in 1967.

units.name: Gate of Hope
units.design_note: No abandoned infants or frightening scenes are drawn; the gate stays closed and never suggests players may enter.
units.historical_fact: From 1854 the convent cared for abandoned baby girls; in 1996 this gate was named the Gate of Hope.

units.name: The Family Side of the Former Hill Street Police Station
units.design_note: The window grid is a recognisable simplification; its count and colour order are not an exact façade record.
units.historical_fact: Completed in 1934, the building housed not only police facilities but also quarters for officers and their families, with a children's playground.

units.name: The Siamese Bronze Elephant outside The Arts House (Old Parliament House)
units.design_note: The sculpture stands as its own object; text appears on separate information labels, and no plinth inscription is faked.
units.historical_fact: The bronze elephant commemorates King Chulalongkorn (Rama V)'s 1871 visit; it was set up in front of the Town Hall in 1872 and moved to today's Arts House in 1919.

units.name: The Benchmark Story at Cavenagh Bridge
units.design_note: The broad arrow is a separate archive icon; the concept position is not on-site navigation to a carved mark.
units.historical_fact: NHB records that the north abutment keeps a survey benchmark from around 1882, marked with a broad arrow and a line to show a known height reference.

units.name: Dalhousie Obelisk
units.design_note: Emphasises the monument's mass; unverified details of its relocation are left out of the art.
units.historical_fact: The obelisk marks the Governor-General's visit in 1850; local merchants including Tan Kim Seng raised the funds and used it to voice their support for free trade.

units.name: The Victoria Clock Tower and the Old Name That Never Left
units.design_note: The clock face serves the public-time theme; the time on its hands carries no historical meaning.
units.historical_fact: The Memorial Hall was renamed Victoria Concert Hall in 1979, yet the old name remains on its outer wall; the central clock tower joins the two buildings.

units.name: Waterfront Public Walkway: Virtual Racing Unlocks the Next Stop
units.design_note: The car and corners in the scene are prototype design, not a survey of a real circuit, and do not represent driving on real roads.
units.historical_fact: The 2026 Singapore Grand Prix runs from 9 to 11 October; the official Connaught Grandstand information links Esplanade Bridge with Turn 14.

units.name: Tan Kim Seng Fountain: The Missing 25 Years
units.design_note: The fountain's form is a thematic concept; 1857 and 1882 are written on separate archive cards, not falsely carved on the structure.
units.historical_fact: In 1857 Tan Kim Seng donated $13,000 to improve the public water supply; the fountain in his memory was put up in 1882.
